group.passage:
In many homes, food is bought with good intentions but never eaten. A bag of vegetables is forgotten at the back of the fridge, or half a loaf of bread goes hard on the kitchen counter. In the end, much of this food is simply [[1]]. This wastes money, of course, but the damage does not stop there.
Growing, packing, and moving food all use large amounts of water, land, and energy. When food is wasted, these resources are wasted too. In addition, food that ends up in a landfill does not simply disappear. As it begins to [[2]], it gives off methane, a gas that adds to global warming. In other words, food waste is bad not only for our wallets but also for the [[3]].
Fortunately, cutting down on food waste at home is not as hard as it sounds, and most of the steps are quite [[4]]. To begin with, it is a good idea to write a shopping [[5]] before going to the supermarket and to buy only what is on it. It is also important to [[6]] food properly so that it lasts longer; for example, bread kept in the freezer can stay good for weeks. Finally, try to [[7]] older vegetables by cooking them into soups or fried rice.
Many people are also [[8]] by the dates printed on food packages. A “best before” date is about quality rather than safety, so food past this date is often still fine to eat. Even fruit that is no longer [[9]] enough to enjoy on its own can be blended into a drink or baked into a cake. Saving food is a [[10]] that anyone can learn, and every small step counts.

translation_zh.text:
在許多家庭裡，食物買回來時是一番好意，最後卻沒有吃掉。一袋蔬菜被遺忘在冰箱深處，或是半條麵包在廚房流理台上變硬。到頭來，這些食物很多都被直接丟掉。這當然浪費錢，但損害還不只如此。
種植、包裝和運送食物都要用掉大量的水、土地和能源。食物被浪費時，這些資源也跟著被浪費。此外，進了垃圾掩埋場的食物並不會就此消失。食物開始腐爛時，會釋放出甲烷，一種會加劇全球暖化的氣體。換句話說，浪費食物不只傷荷包，也傷害環境。
幸好，在家減少食物浪費並沒有聽起來那麼難，大部分的步驟都相當簡單。首先，去超市前最好先寫一張購物清單，而且只買清單上的東西。妥善保存食物、讓它放得更久也很重要；例如，放在冷凍庫裡的麵包可以保存好幾週。最後，試著把放得比較久的蔬菜煮成湯或炒飯用完。
許多人也被食品包裝上印的日期搞糊塗了。「最佳賞味期」標示的是品質而不是安全，所以過了這個日期的食物通常還是可以吃。即使是已經不夠新鮮、不適合直接吃的水果，也可以打成飲料或烤成蛋糕。珍惜食物是任何人都學得會的習慣，而且每一小步都有意義。
